business_summary: Costco runs 939 membership-only warehouse clubs (647 in the US and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 177 elsewhere) plus e-commerce sites in nine countries. It sells a narrow range of bulk groceries, household goods, gasoline, electronics, pharmacy and its own Kirkland Signature brand at a deliberately tiny markup: merchandise gross margin was only 11.09% of net sales in FY2026 (fiscal year ended 2026-08-30). The profit engine is the annual membership fee: 84.1M paid memberships (150.4M cardholders) paid $5.907B of membership fees in FY2026 - equal to ~51% of Costco's $11.685B operating income - and that fee revenue has almost no direct cost attached. Low prices drive loyalty (92.3% US/Canada renewal rate), loyalty drives volume, volume drives buying power and even lower prices. FY2026: total revenue $303.154B (+10.1% net sales), net income $9.226B, diluted EPS $20.76 (incl. a one-off $0.15 tariff-refund benefit). The business is asset-heavy: it owns most of its warehouses and spent $6.435B on capex in FY2026, guiding to ~$7.5B in FY2027 as it opens ~30 net new warehouses a year.

moat.type: Membership-fee flywheel + scale purchasing power + lowest-cost operating model (few SKUs, huge volume per SKU, cheap self-service boxes) + Kirkland Signature private-label brand + member trust/habit (92.3% US/Canada renewal). Competitors cannot match prices without also giving up their margin structure.

quality.revenue_growth_3y: ~7.8% CAGR in total revenue from FY2023 ($242.290B, a 53-week year) to FY2026 ($303.154B); FY2025 $275.235B (+8.2%), FY2026 +10.1% on net sales ($297.247B vs $269.912B). FY2026 adjusted total-company comparable sales (ex gas and FX) +6.6%; management now calls 6-7% comps a 'more normal' pace.
quality.gross_margin: 11.09% of net sales in FY2026 ((net sales $297.247B - merchandise costs $264.279B) / $297.247B); Q4 FY2026 11.02% (-11 bps reported, +20 bps ex-gas). Low by design - Costco caps markups; membership fees ($5.907B, ~100% margin) sit on top. Operating margin 3.85% of total revenue ($11.685B / $303.154B).
quality.roic: ~21% in FY2026: NOPAT ~$8.80B (operating income $11.685B x (1 - 24.7% effective tax rate, $3.025B tax / $12.251B pre-tax)) over invested capital ~$41.97B (equity $35.803B + total debt $6.162B), even with $21.3B of cash sitting in that capital base. Return on average equity ~28% ($9.226B / avg of $35.803B and $29.164B). Excluding excess cash the return on operating capital is materially higher.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: Negative (net cash) - about -1.05x. Cash + short-term investments $21.301B vs long-term debt incl. current portion $6.162B at 2026-08-30 = ~$15.1B net cash; FY2026 EBITDA ~$14.36B (operating income $11.685B + D&A $2.674B). Excludes operating/finance lease liabilities (long-term operating lease liabilities $2.414B).
quality.fcf_positive: yes; FY2026 FCF ~$9.39B (operating cash flow $15.825B - capex $6.435B) = ~$21.13 per diluted share (444.427M shares). Caveat: $2.328B came from favourable working-capital swings (Costco sells inventory before paying suppliers), and FY2027 capex is guided up to ~$7.5B.

valuation.verdict: expensive - price is ~34% above our base fair value and ~15% above even the high end of the band
valuation.method: Equal-weighted blend of two methods via code/valuation.py. (1) P/E: FY2026 diluted EPS $20.76 LESS the one-off $0.15 IEEPA tariff-refund benefit = clean EPS $20.61, x 30 / 35 / 40 = $618.30 / $721.35 / $824.40. Why these multiples: Costco's clean EPS compounded ~13.6%/yr FY2023-FY2026 ($14.16 -> $20.76) and is unusually steady, which earns a premium to MSFT (30x base) and V (28x base) in our other theses - but NOT the post-2020 median of ~45x (computed from Alpaca closes and SEC EPS; 25th percentile ~39.5x, low ~32x). That median was set during a decade of falling rates; with the Fed at 3.75-4.00% and growth guided to normalise to 6-7% comps, we will not underwrite a PEG near 3.5. 40x high = roughly the post-2020 25th percentile; 30x low = below the post-2020 minimum, i.e. a real de-rating. (2) FCF yield: FY2026 FCF per diluted share $21.13 at required yields of 3.8% / 3.2% / 2.7% (same yields as our MSFT thesis; lower than AAPL's because ~60% of Costco's capex is growth capex - capex $6.435B vs D&A $2.674B - so reported FCF understates owner earnings) = $556.05 / $660.31 / $782.59. Blended band $587.18 / $690.83 / $803.50. At $922.76 the stock trades at 44.4x FY2026 GAAP EPS (44.8x clean) and a 2.29% FCF yield.
valuation.trend: Price $922.76 (2026-09-25 close) is below its 50-day average ($934.44) and its 200-day average ($960.38). 52-week closing range $849.75 (2025-12-22) - $1,095.06 (2026-05-19); now ~15.7% below the May high. Stock rose from $896.51 to $922.76 (+2.9%) the day after Q4 results. 6-month return -6.2% vs SPY +21.7% (caller's screen.json). Downtrend is valuation-driven de-rating, not business deterioration.

bull_case: Wide, proven moat: 92.3% US/Canada and 89.8% worldwide renewal rates at FY2026 year-end, with paid memberships +3.8% to 84.1M and Executive (higher-fee) members at 42.3M generating 75.6% of sales. Members keep paying because the warehouse saves them more than the fee.

Membership fees ($5.907B in FY2026, +11.0%) are essentially pure profit and equal ~51% of operating income, giving Costco an annuity-like earnings base that makes profits unusually stable through cycles.

Steady compounding: clean EPS grew from $14.16 (FY2023) to $20.76 (FY2026), ~13.6%/yr; Q4 FY2026 net income ex tariff benefit still grew 12.3%. Traffic is growing (+3.3% Q4 comp traffic), not just ticket.

Long runway: 939 warehouses growing ~25-30 net per year (967 planned by end of FY2027), with international (Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Australia, Europe, China) still early; digitally-enabled comps +20.9% in FY2026 with same-day delivery via DoorDash, Instacart and Uber Eats.
Fortress balance sheet: ~$15.1B net cash; history of special dividends when cash builds (quarterly dividend raised to $1.47). Capital allocation is conservative and shareholder-friendly.
The stock has de-rated from ~$1,095 (May 2026) to ~$923 while the business kept beating - every further de-rating toward ~35x moves a wonderful business toward a buyable price.
risks: VALUATION IS THE THESIS-KILLER. At $922.76 the stock is 44.4x FY2026 EPS and a 2.29% FCF yield, versus a Fed funds rate of 3.75-4.00%. Our base fair value is $690.83; the price is ~34% above it and ~15% above our HIGH case. Even a flawless business can deliver poor returns for years if bought at a peak multiple - that de-rating is exactly what has happened since May (-15.7%).

Growth is normalising: management signaled 6-7% comps are 'a more normal level'; Q4's 9.4% reported comp was flattered by gasoline prices (adjusted 6.7%). Monthly sales deceleration already knocked the stock in July (June comps +8.8% vs May +12.5%).

The membership-fee tailwind is fading: the September 2024 US/Canada fee increase accounted for ~35% of membership-income growth in the first 36 weeks of FY2026; membership-fee growth slowed from +11% in Q3 to +7.3% in Q4 as the increase laps. The timing of the next fee increase is unknown; until then membership-income growth depends on member count and Executive upgrades.

Renewal-rate drift: worldwide renewal slipped as more members sign up online/through digital promotions, which renew at a lower rate (company disclosure). A slow grind down in renewals would hit the highest-margin revenue.

Thin operating margin (3.85%) leaves little room for error: wage and health-care inflation, tariffs ('higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results'), or a price war with Walmart/Sam's Club, Amazon or BJ's would hit earnings disproportionately.

Earnings quality items: Q4 FY2026 EPS included a non-recurring $0.15 tariff-refund benefit; four class actions (filed March 2026) seek to make Costco pass IEEPA tariff refunds to members; FY2026 FCF included $2.328B of working-capital inflow; FY2027 capex rising to ~$7.5B.
Data caveat: FY2026 figures come from the unaudited 8-K earnings release ('subject to reclassification'); the audited FY2026 10-K is expected in October 2026 and must be re-checked.
what_would_break_thesis: US/Canada membership renewal rate falls below 90.0% for two consecutive quarterly reports (it is 92.3% at FY2026 year-end; 92.2% at Q3).
Worldwide renewal rate falls below 87.0% (89.8% now).
Paid memberships decline year-over-year in any quarterly report (84.1M, +3.8% now).
Membership fee revenue declines year-over-year (ex-FX) in any quarter - the moat's cash register shrinking.
Adjusted total-company comparable sales (ex gas and FX) below +2% for two consecutive quarters (+6.7% in Q4 FY2026; +6.6% FY2026).
Full-year operating margin (operating income / total revenue) falls below 3.0% (3.85% in FY2026) - a sign of a price war or cost structure breaking.
Net cash (~$15.1B) turns into net debt above 1.0x EBITDA, or a large debt-funded acquisition that departs from the warehouse model.
Operating cash flow fails to cover capex for a full fiscal year (FY2026 OCF $15.825B vs capex $6.435B).
Any serious accounting red flag, restatement, material weakness in internal controls, or auditor change.
PRICE DISCIPLINE (entry rule, not a sell rule): do not initiate or add above $691 (base fair value). A first small tranche is only justified below ~$620 (~10% under base, about 30x clean EPS).
catalysts: Audited FY2026 Form 10-K (expected October 2026) - confirm the press-release numbers, finance-lease totals, and any new risk disclosures.
Monthly sales reports (early each month) and Q1 FY2027 results (expected mid-December 2026): watch adjusted comps vs the 6-7% 'normal' guide and membership-fee growth after the fee-increase lap.

A continued de-rating toward ~30-35x EPS (roughly $620-$720) - the only thing that makes this ownable under our rules; it requires a further ~22-33% decline, which historically has needed a broad market sell-off or a growth scare.
A special dividend (Costco has paid them when cash builds; $20.2B cash at FY2026 year-end) or the renewal of the $4.0B buyback authorization that expires January 2027.
Resolution of the IEEPA tariff-refund class actions (motions to dismiss pending).
